answer: Each agent periodically presents a signed proof‑of‑work that includes a fresh hash of its identity token mirrored against a public basalt ledger, while the token itself is an onyx‑colored nonce derived from a hardware‑bound TPM. A randomly drawn jury of validators audits a statistically chosen subset of these proofs, and any mismatch triggers an immediate revocation broadcast. Because forging a unique hardware bound nonce and bribing enough jurors costs linear resources with the size of the Sybil set, an attacker must expend prohibitive computational and monetary effort for each fake identity.
